ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Ernest Shackleton

code.originalText: Six-week review: angina on medical therapy, smoking, and a shared decision about coronary angiography and stenting

text.paragraph: Six-week review of angina on medical therapy; decision about coronary angiography. [S]

Mr. Shackleton returns four weeks after his consultation. On metoprolol 100 mg his resting pulse is 60, but he still has chest tightness two or three times a week when he climbs the stairs carrying papers or walks fast into a cold wind, and he has used nitroglycerin four times. It never comes at rest. He has not smoked for five weeks. He is drinking within the limit he agreed. He sails in under three months, will be lifting and hauling at sea, and will be weeks from a hospital. He asked whether a stent would let him do that. He was uneasy about having a procedure that the backers might hear of, and said so; after talking it through he wants to go ahead. [S]

value.displayName: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with other forms of angina pectoris

list.item:
Chronic coronary disease with stable angina despite medical therapy (I25.118). Angina persists at class II despite a beta-blocker at a dose that holds his resting pulse at 60, with aspirin and a high-intensity statin. The options were explained: add a long-acting nitrate, amlodipine, or ranolazine; or coronary angiography and a stent to the proximal LAD lesion, which has a CT-FFR of 0.70. In stable coronary disease with normal heart function, a stent relieves angina better than medicines alone but does not lower the risk of heart attack or death. It means aspirin with clopidogrel for six months, which raises the risk of bleeding from injuries at sea. He chose angiography and a stent because he wants to work hard and haul loads on the expedition without angina, and he accepts the bleeding risk. Dr. Solberg-Adebayo agrees. Pre-procedure tests today: creatinine 0.96 mg/dL (eGFR 98), potassium 4.3 mmol/L, hemoglobin 15.6 g/dL, platelets 245 thousand per microliter. [S]
Coronary angiography by the right radial artery with a stent to the proximal LAD as a day case next week.
Clopidogrel 600 mg loading dose before the procedure, then 75 mg daily for six months with aspirin.
Continue metoprolol 100 mg, atorvastatin 80 mg, and nitroglycerin as needed.

Nicotine dependence, cigarettes (F17.210). Abstinent for five weeks. [S]
Continue varenicline.
